concepts.name: Middle Eastern Languages
concepts.scope: Study of Semitic, Iranian, Turkic, and other languages of the Middle East, including their historical relationships, scripts, and sociocultural use.

concepts.name: Western European Languages
concepts.scope: Study of French, German, Iberian, Italian, Latin, and Classical Greek languages, excluding English, with attention to their varieties, histories, and teaching.

concepts.name: Early English Languages
concepts.scope: Historical and philological study of Old, Middle, and Early Modern English, including language change, manuscripts, spelling, and historical usage.

concepts.name: English Language
concepts.scope: Advanced study of contemporary English varieties, grammar, vocabulary, discourse conventions, usage, and regional or social variation.

concepts.name: English as a Second Language
concepts.scope: Research and practice concerning English acquisition, second-language teaching, learner difficulties, assessment, curriculum, and intercultural classroom use.

concepts.name: Translation and Interpretation Studies
concepts.scope: Theory, practice, technology, ethics, and quality problems in written translation, oral interpreting, localization, and cross-language mediation.

concepts.name: Central and Eastern European Languages
concepts.scope: Study of the languages of Central and Eastern Europe, including Slavic, Baltic, and Uralic language traditions.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander literature), Book history, British and Irish literature, Central and Eastern European literature (incl. Russian), Children's literature, Comparative and transnational literature, Digital literature, Ecocriticism, Indian literature
clusters.division_scope: Communication and media studies, Cultural studies, Language studies, Linguistics, Literary studies
clusters.boundary: This domain excludes communication processes and media institutions, broad cultural practices and identity politics, general language study, and formal linguistic analysis, which belong respectively to Communication and Media Studies, Cultural Studies, Language Studies, and Linguistics.

concepts.name: Literary Theory
concepts.scope: Concepts and debates about literariness, interpretation, canon formation, authorship, narrative, genre, and the social functions of literature.

concepts.name: Stylistics and Textual Analysis
concepts.scope: Close and formal analysis of diction, syntax, rhetoric, narrative structure, voice, meter, and other features of literary texts.

concepts.name: Book History and Print Culture
concepts.scope: The material production, publication, circulation, preservation, readership, and historical transformation of books and print objects.

concepts.name: Digital Literature
concepts.scope: Literary works created, distributed, or experienced through computational and networked media, including electronic, hypertext, and generative forms.

concepts.name: Comparative and Transnational Literature
concepts.scope: Cross-linguistic and cross-cultural study of literary forms, movements, themes, translation, circulation, and transnational literary relations.

concepts.name: Ecocriticism
concepts.scope: Literary study of environmental imagination, human–nonhuman relations, climate change, ecological crisis, and environmental justice.

concepts.name: Children's and Young Adult Literature
concepts.scope: Literature addressed primarily to children or adolescents, including its forms, readerships, institutions, pedagogies, and cultural representations.

concepts.name: Popular and Genre Literature
concepts.scope: Mass and commercial literary forms organized by genre conventions, including crime, romance, science fiction, fantasy, horror, and speculative fiction.

concepts.name: World Literatures
concepts.scope: National, regional, and multilingual literary traditions across Africa, the Americas, Europe, Asia, the Middle East, Australia, and New Zealand.

concepts.name: Postcolonial Literatures
concepts.scope: Literatures shaped by colonialism, decolonization, empire, diaspora, hybridity, nationalism, and resistance, especially in formerly colonized societies.

clusters.scope: Bioethics, Business ethics, Ethical use of new technology, Human rights and justice issues (excl. law), Legal ethics, Medical ethics, Professional ethics
clusters.division_scope: Applied ethics, History and philosophy of specific fields, Philosophy, Religious studies, Theology
clusters.boundary: This domain excludes abstract philosophy, historical or philosophical studies of particular fields, and religious or theological approaches, which belong respectively to Philosophy, History and philosophy of specific fields, Religious studies, and Theology.

concepts.name: Bioethics
concepts.scope: Ethical issues in life sciences, biotechnology, human enhancement, reproduction, genetics, disability, and end-of-life decisions, excluding clinical practice and research governance.

concepts.name: Business ethics
concepts.scope: Moral responsibilities of firms and markets, including corporate accountability, stakeholder relations, sustainability, labor practices, and commercial integrity.

concepts.name: Ethical use of new technology
concepts.scope: Normative evaluation of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, automation, digital systems, surveillance, data practices, and technological design.

concepts.name: Legal ethics
concepts.scope: Professional duties, conflicts of interest, confidentiality, advocacy, adjudication, and institutional integrity within legal practice.

concepts.name: Medical ethics
concepts.scope: Ethical problems in clinical care, including informed consent, confidentiality, professional authority, treatment refusal, clinical decision-making, and patient vulnerability.

concepts.name: Professional ethics
concepts.scope: Norms of conduct, competence, accountability, conflicts of interest, and public responsibility across occupations other than legal practice.

concepts.name: Research Ethics
concepts.scope: Ethical governance of biomedical, social, and behavioral research, including informed consent, risk assessment, participant protection, research integrity, and responsible authorship.

concepts.name: Public Health Ethics
concepts.scope: Population-level ethical problems involving prevention, health promotion, epidemiological surveillance, resource allocation, quarantine, and protection of vulnerable communities.

concepts.name: Ethical Deliberation Methods
concepts.scope: Applied procedures for resolving concrete moral conflicts, including principled analysis, casuistry, reflective equilibrium, stakeholder deliberation, and ethics consultation.

concepts.name: Environmental Ethics
concepts.scope: Ethical issues concerning human relationships with animals, ecosystems, biodiversity, and the natural environment.

clusters.cluster: History and philosophy of specific fields
clusters.scope: History and philosophy of engineering and technology, History and philosophy of law and justice, History and philosophy of medicine, History and philosophy of science, History and philosophy of the humanities, History and philosophy of the social sciences, History of ideas, History of philosophy
clusters.division_scope: Applied ethics, History and philosophy of specific fields, Philosophy, Religious studies, Theology
clusters.boundary: It deliberately excludes standalone systematic philosophy, normative applied ethics, religious traditions, and theological doctrines, which belong to Philosophy, Applied Ethics, Religious Studies, and Theology.

concepts.name: History and Philosophy of Engineering and Technology
concepts.scope: Historical development and philosophical analysis of engineering practices, technological artifacts, design, innovation, and human-technology relations.

concepts.name: History and Philosophy of Law and Justice
concepts.scope: Historical and conceptual study of legal institutions, jurisprudence, adjudication, punishment, rights, and changing ideas of justice.

concepts.name: History and Philosophy of Medicine
concepts.scope: Historical and philosophical examination of medical theories, clinical practices, diagnostic categories, healing institutions, and conceptions of health and disease.

concepts.name: History and Philosophy of Science
concepts.scope: Historical reconstruction and philosophical analysis of scientific practices, theories, evidence, explanation, rationality, and scientific change.

concepts.name: History and Philosophy of the Humanities
concepts.scope: Study of the historical formation, methods, interpretive practices, and epistemic status of disciplines such as literature, history, and the arts.

concepts.name: History and Philosophy of the Social Sciences
concepts.scope: Historical and philosophical analysis of social-scientific concepts, methods, explanatory models, disciplines, and disputes over objectivity and interpretation.

concepts.name: History of Ideas
concepts.scope: Intellectual history tracing the emergence, transmission, transformation, and cultural circulation of concepts across societies and fields.

concepts.name: History of Philosophical Traditions
concepts.scope: Historical study of philosophical schools, texts, arguments, traditions, and their development across periods and intellectual contexts.

concepts.name: Global History of Philosophy
concepts.scope: Comparative and transregional histories of philosophical thought across European, Asian, African, Islamic, Indigenous, and other intellectual traditions.

concepts.name: Philosophical Historiography
concepts.scope: Theory and methodology of writing the history of philosophy, including contextualization, periodization, interpretation, canon formation, and historical explanation.

clusters.scope: Aesthetics, Critical theory, Decision theory, Environmental philosophy, Epistemology, Ethical theory, Hermeneutics, Logic, Metaphysics, Phenomenology
clusters.division_scope: Applied ethics, History and philosophy of specific fields, Philosophy, Religious studies, Theology
clusters.boundary: This domain excludes applied ethical policy and professional cases, the history and philosophy of specific sciences or fields, religious studies, and theology, which belong to Applied Ethics, History and Philosophy of Specific Fields, Religious Studies, and Theology respectively.

concepts.name: Aesthetics
concepts.scope: Philosophical theories of beauty, artistic value, aesthetic experience, interpretation, and the nature of art.

concepts.name: Critical Theory
concepts.scope: Philosophical analysis of ideology, domination, social power, emancipation, and the normative conditions of social critique.

concepts.name: Normative Decision Theory
concepts.scope: Formal accounts of rational choice, preference, utility, risk, uncertainty, and action under deliberative constraints.

concepts.name: Epistemology
concepts.scope: Theories of knowledge, belief, justification, evidence, skepticism, testimony, and epistemic norms.

concepts.name: Ethical Theory
concepts.scope: General theories of moral value, obligation, virtue, reasons for action, and the foundations of normative judgment.

concepts.name: Hermeneutics
concepts.scope: Theories and methods of interpretation, understanding, textual meaning, historical situatedness, and the interpretive circle.

concepts.name: Logic
concepts.scope: Formal and philosophical study of consequence, validity, proof, inference, consistency, and the structure of reasoning.

concepts.name: Metaphysics
concepts.scope: Philosophical investigation of being, reality, identity, modality, causation, universals, time, and dependence.

concepts.name: Phenomenology
concepts.scope: Systematic description of first-person experience, intentionality, embodiment, temporality, consciousness, and lived-world structures.

concepts.name: Poststructuralism
concepts.scope: Philosophical analyses of discourse, difference, subject formation, textual instability, genealogy, and the critique of fixed structures.
